# Finding the Antiderivative of ∫ 3·eˣ·sin(x) dx

## Using Integration by Parts (Twice)

Let me compute I = ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx first, then multiply by 3.

**First integration by parts:**
- u = sin(x), dv = exp(x)dx
- du = cos(x)dx, v = exp(x)

I = exp(x)·sin(x) − ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx

**Second integration by parts** (on ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx):
- u = cos(x), dv = exp(x)dx
- du = −sin(x)dx, v = exp(x)

∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx = exp(x)·cos(x) + ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx = exp(x)·cos(x) + I

**Substituting back:**

I = exp(x)·sin(x) − exp(x)·cos(x) − I

2*I = exp(x)·sin(x) − exp(x)·cos(x)

I = exp(x)·(sin(x) − cos(x)) / 2

## Multiplying by 3

∫ 3·exp(x)·sin(x) dx = 3·exp(x)·(sin(x) − cos(x)) / 2 + C

## Verification

d/dx [3·exp(x)·(sin(x) − cos(x)) / 2]
= (3/2)·exp(x)·(sin(x) − cos(x)) + (3/2)·exp(x)·(cos(x) + sin(x))
= (3/2)·exp(x)·[sin(x) − cos(x) + cos(x) + sin(x)]
= (3/2)·exp(x)·[2·sin(x)]
= 3·exp(x)·sin(x) ✓

<answer>3*exp(x)*(sin(x) - cos(x))/2 + C</answer>
